# Purpose

These sessions teach the **principles of reproducible research** — transparency, provenance, and documentation that outlives the project — together with the everyday **workflows** that put them into practice.

Students organise a project folder and write documentation for **their own PhD project**, then transfer that text into the course assignment's Swedish Research Council DMP template.

<!-- This is AI-slop and can be removed.

The folder and the DMP are the **vehicle, not the subject**: every activity names the principle it serves, and readiness tests stay conceptual, so students can justify their choices in a project we never saw rather than copy a folder tree.

-->

Success criterion — the **5-year test**: someone returning in five years, the student or a colleague, can understand what was done and which decisions were made. It is methodology-agnostic and must hold for qualitative, survey, trial, and secondary-data projects alike.

Teaching time is **two afternoons of Team-Based Learning (3 h each)**, each preceded by a guided self-study morning (3 h). Day 1 afternoon is hybrid (room Future + Zoom), Day 2 is Zoom-only, so every team activity must work in breakout rooms. Those are the constraints everything else is sized against.

# Learning outcomes

By the end of the two days, the student can:

1.  **Explain** the principles of reproducible and open research — transparency, provenance, raw versus derived material, FAIR versus open — and use them to justify choices in their own project.
2.  **Structure** a durable project folder and its documentation (README, decision log, naming and versioning) so the project passes the 5-year test.
3.  **Track** changes and decisions using that humans and tools can both read, and justify which approach fits their project.
4.  **Draft** the documentation, data description, and storage answers of the Swedish Research Council DMP template from their own project package.
5.  **Judge** what can be shared, what must stay protected, and how to use KI-supported AI tools (Copilot-first) responsibly — with disclosure and verification.

<!-- Students will not hand in anything to us who run these two days, they will only work on their own projects and DMP
Outcomes 2–4 are evidenced by the material students hand in; outcomes 1 and 5 by readiness tests, peer critique, and a short AI-use disclosure.

# Scope boundaries (the point of this lock)

**In scope:** the principles of reproducible and open research, and the workflows that enact them — folder structure, documentation, decision traceability, sharing boundaries, responsible AI use, and the DMP sections these feed.
